title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Pula, Croatia: 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Does Pula have all-inclusive hotels? Yes, a few in Verudela. See what's included, 2027 price estimates per person, and who should self-cater instead.
content:
## Does Pula Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes, but the offer is small. Pula is mainly a city-break and apartment destination, so all-inclusive is a niche product. It is concentrated in one place: the Verudela peninsula, a pine-covered resort zone about 3 km south of the Arena amphitheatre. The old town, the Riva waterfront and the Stoja area have no true all-inclusive hotels. They have hotels with breakfast or half-board and many private apartments.

Three Park Plaza properties in Verudela are the ones most often listed with all-inclusive options: Park Plaza Arena Pula, Park Plaza Histria Pula and Park Plaza Verudela Pula (a mix of studio apartments and villas). Splendid Resort, also in Verudela, appears in tour-operator all-inclusive programmes. The luxury Grand Hotel Brioni Pula (a Radisson Collection hotel) is sold with breakfast and half-board, not all-inclusive.

Board plans change by season and by operator. A hotel may sell all-inclusive only through a package or only in July and August. Confirm the exact plan on the booking page before paying.

## What Is Usually Included

The all-inclusive plans at Pula resorts are generally lighter than the Mediterranean "ultra" model:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner, mostly buffet
- Local house wine, beer, soft drinks and water with meals, and often at the bar during set hours
- Afternoon snacks or ice cream at some properties
- Pool, beach access and a kids' club in high season

Usually not included: premium spirits, à la carte restaurants, spa treatments, sun loungers on some beaches, and the tourist tax (about €1.50–2 per adult per night). Verudela's all-inclusive is a convenience plan, not a party plan.

## Price Per Person Per Night (Estimates)

These are rough per-person figures based on current double-room rates of about €200–240 per room per night at the Park Plaza hotels in early September, with the room price adjusted for the board plan. Rates vary widely by date and booking channel.

| Option | Shoulder (May–June, September) | Peak (July–August) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive, 4-star Verudela hotel | €65–95 | €100–140 |
| Half-board, same hotel type | €50–75 | €75–110 |
| Bed and breakfast, same hotel type | €40–60 | €60–95 |
| Private apartment (family of 4, room only) | €15–25 | €25–45 |
| Apartment plus groceries and restaurant dinners | €40–55 | €55–80 |

All-inclusive costs about 25–40% more than half-board. Compared with an apartment, it costs two to four times as much for the accommodation alone. Children's discounts are significant: kids under 12 commonly pay 0–50% of the adult rate, and this changes the calculation for families.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Pula

### Families with small children

This is the best case. Verudela has pools, kids' pools, kids' clubs and short walks to shallow pebble and rock-platform beaches. Buffet meals at fixed times remove the daily question of where to eat with a toddler. Children-free-or-discounted deals make the total reasonable, and the on-site setting means no car is needed.

### Short stays of 3–5 nights

For a short beach break, all-inclusive or half-board avoids shopping and cooking for a few days. The value is highest when the stay is built around the resort itself and not around sightseeing.

### Who should self-cater

Visitors who plan to explore are better off in an apartment. Pula's main sights, including the Arena, Temple of Augustus and Forum, are in the old town, 3 km from Verudela. Anyone eating out in town at lunch will not use the lunch buffet they have paid for. Groups of adults who prefer konobas, couples on a city break and stays of more than a week are cheaper and more flexible with an apartment.

A direct opinion: for adults without children, all-inclusive in Pula is poor value. Local restaurants and markets are good and inexpensive, and a self-catering base costs a third of the resort price.

## All-Inclusive Outside Pula

If Verudela's options are sold out or too limited, the nearest alternatives are:

- **Medulin**, about 10 km south: Ai Pini Medulin Resort and other resorts with board plans, in a sandier, more beach-focused area.
- **Plava Laguna, Poreč**, about 55–60 km north-west: Hotel Albatros and Hotel Aurora are known for all-inclusive and animation programmes.
- **Rabac**, about 45–50 km north-east: Valamar properties including Bellevue Resort and Girandella Resort are listed with all-inclusive options.

Check plans in each case, since they vary by year.

## Practical Tips

- Book all-inclusive through tour operators for UK and German markets. Package rates are often lower than the hotel's own site.
- Ask what the drinks window is. Some plans stop at 23:00 or only cover house brands.
- Verudela has small shops and a few restaurants within walking distance, so half-board plus one dinner out is a flexible middle option.
- The bus from Verudela to the centre takes about 15 minutes. A taxi is typically €8–12. Walking along the coast path takes about 40 minutes.
- Shoulder season is pleasant for swimming in June and September, with sea temperatures of about 22–24 °C, and rates are 30–40% lower than in August.

## FAQ

See the questions below for quick answers.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Pula?
faq.answer: Yes. The Park Plaza hotels in Verudela (Arena, Histria and Verudela) are listed with all-inclusive options, and Splendid Resort appears in tour-operator programmes. Availability depends on season and booking channel.

faq.question: How much is all-inclusive in Pula per person per night?
faq.answer: Roughly €65–95 per person in shoulder season and €100–140 in July and August for a 4-star resort in double occupancy. These are estimates, and child discounts can reduce the family total significantly.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive or half-board better in Pula?
faq.answer: Half-board is better for most adults, because it costs about 25–40% less and leaves lunch free for sightseeing in the old town. All-inclusive is better for families with small children who stay mainly at the resort.

faq.question: Is an apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Pula?
faq.answer: Yes, in most cases. A family of four in a private apartment typically pays €15–25 per person per night in shoulder season and €25–45 in peak season for the room alone. Even with groceries and some restaurant meals, the total is usually lower.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive outside Pula?
faq.answer: Medulin is the closest, about 10 km from Pula. Plava Laguna near Poreč (about 55–60 km) and Rabac (about 45–50 km) also have hotels with all-inclusive plans.

quickAnswer: Yes, Pula has all-inclusive options, almost all in the Verudela resort area 3 km south of the centre. Park Plaza Arena, Park Plaza Histria and Park Plaza Verudela sell all-inclusive or similar board plans. Expect roughly €65–95 per person per night in shoulder season and €100–140 in peak season.
